analysis.title: US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing Oct 14
key_insights: SPX -1.1%, NDX -2.0%, RTY -1.9% on Oct 14. SPX ended a 53-day streak without a 1%+ decline. RTY is 11% below its peak and in a correction.

The initial selloff came from the hotter-than-expected September core CPI, but tech was the main driver of the day's decline. Cyclicals underperformed Defensives by 7.0%, with healthcare and staples outperforming.

Treasuries sold off at the 8:30am ET CPI release, with the 2Y spiking nearly 16bp, then reversed almost entirely by the close (2Y +2bp, 10Y -2bp, 30Y -4bp). October hike probability moved from ~20% to ~50% after CPI, then fell back to ~33%.

JPM saw no clear catalyst or dovish signal behind the yield reversal. Its three reasons: wait for Thursday's PPI and Fedspeak before reading a Fed signal into yields, the market overreacted when October hike odds went above 50%, and there was a move into quality and safe assets with concern about a possible AI-related credit event.
About 30bp of hikes are priced through year-end.

AI was again the main challenge. Semis, memory and hardware sold off. ASML fell 3.9% despite a beat-and-raise, and CoreWeave fell 15.5% as its 2032 unsecured bonds moved into distress. A headline on an OpenAI staff departure intensified the selloff.

SOXX fell for a sixth straight day, with financing risks and IPO timelines at the center of the story. JPM thinks memories of the July selloff played a part, with investors possibly de-grossing ahead of IPO-related updates.

JPM positioning data: tech positioning (TPM) is at a neutral ~46th percentile, versus ~19th percentile near the late-July low. JPM sees potential for further de-grossing into key tech catalysts but stays constructive on the sector and sees a possible dip-buying opportunity.

September core CPI unrounded was +0.335% m/m, above the Street's 0.2% and Feroli's 0.18%. The increase was broad across categories, with used cars, transportation and apparel standing out. Chase card data and bank earnings show consumer spending remains elevated, keeping core inflation sticky.

JPM Econ (Abiel Reinhart) forecasts core PCE at 0.31% m/m (3.1% y/y, 2.8% 3m saar), firm enough to put the October FOMC in play. JPM still expects the next Fed hike in December. Core goods rose 0.25%, core services 0.37%, supercore 0.42%, and the three-month core goods pace of 2.2% is near last year's highs.
Headline CPI exceeded swap market pricing by over 7bp, the largest upside surprise since the March 2024 CPI report. The broader run of inflation surprises now points to upside for inflation markets.

BAC missed on topline by about 3%, driven by fee income, and fell about 5%. Equities revenue missed by 1.5% and FICC by 10%. Total trading was -5% y/y versus GS +37%, C +6% and JPM +15%. Financials desk (Rob O'Dwyer) expects the market to pressure BAC management on the call.
Financials desk (Taylor Barry) reports a client complaint that Financials get sold both when AI rallies (flow of funds, seen as AI losers) and when AI fades (exposure to AI financing).

Tech desk (Nick Gallo): SMH was down 80bp pre-market while Mag 7 kept pushing higher as models become interchangeable at the frontier. Higher rates benefit hyperscalers that can lean on FCF. The desk saw a noticeable uptick in Mag 7 demand the day before.
ASML posted a strong quarter with margins well ahead of expectations and a higher Q4 guide. Customers are placing orders as far out as 2030 and the company plans to increase supply capacity.

DPZ: the JPM analyst remains Overweight with a Dec-27 PT of $350. Guidance reflects an expected reduction in unit growth. Restaurant positioning is extremely low, with an L/S ratio of 0.5x at the 1st percentile since 2018.

ETF desk (Jonathan Rogerson): customers have been buying energy (MLPA, MLPX, AMLP, IEO), growth (a large IWF block, with offers wanted in VUG and VONG) and DRAM on dips. International products face supply as dollar strength weighs, and the desk expects that to extend after CPI.

PPI and Retail Sales on Oct 15: Feroli sees headline PPI +0.5% m/m (5.3% y/y) and core +0.3% (4.4% y/y), with Food PPI at 0.7%. He sees headline Retail Sales +0.4% and the control group +0.2%, driven by Chase card data.

JPM US Market Intel remains Tactically Bullish into earnings. The SOX is about 20% off its July lows and about 15% below its June all-time highs. Breadth is deteriorating, but JPM expects it to reverse into or out of earnings season.

JPM's Monetization Menu (Oct 12) prefers Tech and some Cyclicals, with AI a globally bullish theme. It suggests Cruise Lines, Hotels and Retailers from the COVID Reopening theme, and likes Brazil and Japan outside AI.

Prior menus (Oct 5, Sep 28) no longer pair a Tech long with an RTY short because of squeeze risk from lower oil or yields. They favor Banks ex-AI and see a US/Iran deal as the biggest catalyst, squeezing EU and RTY higher.
Europe closed mostly higher (UKX +0.7%, SX5E +0.4%, SXXP +0.4%, DAX +0.2%). EZU closed -0.8%, outperforming major US indices. UK homebuilders, defence, luxury and defensives led.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 topline missed by about 3% on fee income, with equities down 1.5% and FICC down 10% versus expectations. Trading revenue fell 5% y/y versus peers up. The stock fell about 5%.
Strong quarter with margins well ahead of expectations and a higher Q4 guide. Customers are ordering as far out as 2030. The stock still fell 3.9%.
Shares fell 15.5% as its 2032 unsecured bonds moved into distress.
Analyst keeps Overweight and the Dec-27 PT after earnings. Guidance reflects a slowdown in unit growth, and the focus is on free cash flow.

sector_views.rationale: Tactically bullish. Semis, memory and Mag 7 preferred, and JPM sees dip-buying opportunity despite possible further de-grossing.
The desk calls the sector sloppy after BAC's miss. Banks were preferred ex-AI in earlier menus on growth and capital markets.
Cruise Lines, Hotels and Retailers are on the shopping list given consumer strength and insulation from elevated energy prices.
Rate-sensitive sectors may join a squeeze but are likely to lag the SPX ex-AI plays.

earnings_insights: BAC Q3 (reported 10/14): topline about 3% below consensus on fee income. Equities revenue missed by 1.5%, FICC by 10%, and total trading was -5% y/y versus GS +37%, C +6% and JPM +15%. Expenses also missed, with noise from AML issues.
ASML Q3 (reported 10/14): margins well ahead of expectations and the Q4 guide raised, with orders placed as far out as 2030.
DPZ (reported 10/13): guidance reflects reduced unit growth. Analyst keeps Overweight and the Dec-27 PT of $350.
Upcoming earnings 10/15: AA, BNY, IBKR, JBHT, MRSH, PLD, PNC, SCHW, USB. 10/16: CFG, TFC, TRV.

Spike in bond vol or equity vol.
Hotter inflation raising the odds of October and 2027 Fed hikes.
A stronger dollar weighing on international ETFs.
vol_and_positioning: TPM (tech positioning) sits at a neutral ~46th percentile, versus ~19th percentile near the late-July low. JPM sees potential for further de-grossing into key tech catalysts.
US positioning was largely unchanged month to date.
Restaurants positioning is extremely low, with L/S ratio at 0.5x, the 1st percentile since 2018, and shorts outpacing longs.
Banks positioning got longer into earnings per the prime book, though the desk did not see it in flow.
Bond vol and equity vol spikes are listed as a risk.
geopolitical: Container ship sank in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran war attacks continue (CNBC link).
A US/Iran deal is flagged as the biggest catalyst for squeezing EU and RTY higher.
The trade truce between Trump and Xi expires Nov 1, with a reported extension through Jan 20, 2027.
IMF-World Bank Annual Meeting in Bangkok Oct 12-18, with Warsh giving final remarks before the FOMC.
US midterm election Nov 3, Brazil runoff Oct 25, Israel legislative election Oct 27.

tension_points.bull_case: JPM stays tactically bullish. Semis can climb the wall of worry as Hynix and Samsung updates show ongoing thematic strength, and earnings and breadth recovery should support the rally.
tension_points.bear_case: SOXX fell six straight days, with financing risks, IPO timelines and AI credit fears (CoreWeave bonds in distress). Positioning at the 46th percentile versus the 19th percentile at the July low leaves room for further de-grossing.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Tech earnings miss, AI credit spread widening, or a spike in bond or equity vol.

tension_points.bull_case: Odds of an October hike fell back to ~33%, and a dovish PPI or inflation print could remove hike expectations and lower yields.
tension_points.bear_case: Core CPI beat broadly, JPM expects core PCE of 0.31%, and consumer spending remains elevated, keeping the 2027 hike probability elevated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A hot PPI print on Oct 15 would confirm the PCE read-through and push October hike odds higher.
